layers.name: Backend API Layer
layers.description: HTTP route handlers and controllers for SmartSave's REST API endpoints, implementing budget, transaction, goal, analytics, auth, and financial advisor APIs

layers.name: Backend Data Layer
layers.description: Mongoose data models (User, Transaction, Budget, Goal, etc.), database configuration, and server entry point for the SmartSave backend

layers.name: Backend Services & Middleware Layer
layers.description: Business logic services (AI advisor, notifications, recurring transactions, queues), middleware (auth, validation, rate limiting, error handling), and utility functions (helpers, audit, email, money, logger)

layers.name: Backend Infrastructure & Config
layers.description: Docker build and compose files, environment configuration, PM2 ecosystem, package.json, and upload directory for the SmartSave backend

layers.name: Frontend UI Layer
layers.description: Flutter screens, widgets, and providers for SmartSave's UI including dashboard, analytics, budget, goals, transactions, financial advisor, and gamification screens

layers.name: Frontend Data & Domain Layer
layers.description: Dart data models, repository implementations, remote/local datasources, domain repository interfaces, and use cases following clean architecture for the Flutter app

layers.name: Frontend App Core Layer
layers.description: Flutter app entry point, app shell and routing, dependency injection, network client, theme system, constants, error handling, and cross-cutting services (cache, auth, export, sync)

layers.name: Frontend Platform & Config Layer

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what SmartSave is — a personal finance & savings application with a Node.js/Express/MongoDB backend and a Flutter/Dart frontend. This gives you the high-level purpose, architecture stack, and project structure before diving into code.

tour.title: Backend Entry Point and Configuration
tour.description: Explore the backend's server entry point (server.js) and configuration module (config/index.js, config/database.js). server.js bootstraps Express middleware, connects routes, and starts the HTTP server. The config module loads environment variables and sets up the MongoDB connection via Mongoose — the foundation everything else depends on.

tour.title: Backend Data Models
tour.description: The Mongoose data models define the schema and behavior for all domain entities. Transaction.js, User.js, Budget.js, and Goal.js are the most heavily imported models, forming the core data layer that controllers, services, and middleware all depend on.

tour.title: Backend API Layer — Controllers and Routes
tour.description: Controllers handle business logic for each feature endpoint (transactions, budgets, goals, analytics, auth, etc.), while route files wire them to Express HTTP paths. This is the layer that receives HTTP requests, validates input, calls models/services, and sends responses back to the client.

tour.title: Backend Middleware and Services
tour.description: Middleware (auth.js, errorHandler.js, validate.js, catchAsync.js) cross-cuts every request with authentication, validation, error handling, and rate limiting. Services (aiService, notificationService, recurringService) contain the core business logic. The high fan-in of auth.js and catchAsync.js shows how foundational these are to the backend.

tour.title: Frontend Entry Point and App Shell
tour.description: main.dart is the Flutter entry point — it initializes Firebase, sets up dependency injection via service_locator.dart, wraps the app in MultiProvider with 16 state providers, and launches the app widget. app.dart and routes.dart define the MaterialApp shell and named route configuration.

tour.title: Frontend UI Screens and Widgets
tour.description: The screen files (dashboard_screen.dart, analytics_screen.dart, budget_screen.dart, etc.) are the highest fan-out nodes in the frontend, each importing many providers, models, and widgets. The shared widgets (chart_card, insight_card, metric_card, custom_text_field) are reusable UI components composed across screens.

tour.title: Frontend State Management — Providers
tour.description: Providers (auth_provider.dart, budget_provider.dart, transaction_provider.dart, etc.) are the state management layer using Flutter's Provider pattern. Each provider encapsulates the state and business logic for a feature domain, connects to repositories, and exposes data to screens via ChangeNotifier. The BFS from main.dart shows providers as the first layer imported after the entry point.

tour.title: Frontend Data Layer — Repositories, Models, Datasources
tour.description: Following clean architecture, the data layer separates concerns into domain repositories (interfaces), data repositories (implementations), data models (JSON serialization), and remote/local datasources. This structure allows the UI to remain decoupled from API and persistence details.

tour.title: Infrastructure and Configuration
tour.description: The infrastructure layer ties everything together: Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml for containerized deployment, package.json for backend dependencies, pubspec.yaml for Flutter dependencies, environment configuration (.env.example), and platform-specific files (Android Manifest, iOS Info.plist, Gradle configs). These files are essential for building, running, and deploying SmartSave.

meta.projectDescription: SmartSave - Personal Finance & Savings Application API. A cross-platform mobile application for tracking expenses, analyzing spending habits, and achieving savings goals. Large project with 292 files across backend (Node.js/Express/MongoDB) and frontend (Flutter/Dart) codebases.
